column1: # What the TXT-05 prototype writes over the arrival sequence (the first thing a new game
# shows: research/renderer-runtime.md § "Reaching the first dialogue"). Tab-separated.
#   site    a line id (research/text-format.md § "Proposed line id"); every physical copy is written
#   source  a line id in translation/samples/ (its English is read from there), or `fixture`
#   label   yes = prefix the sample's speaker, "Boku: ..."
#   wrap    yes = break lines at spaces to the band's width; no = leave the page as written
#   text    fixtures only: layout tests, not translation. ` // ` is a page break, \n a line break
# The English here is not the translation of these sites: the prototype writes in place, so
# each site takes a sample line that fits its bytes and has its page count. Messages of the
# sequence that are not listed (E0177.0, E0179 onward) stay Japanese on purpose: they show that
# untranslated text keeps its cells and its 14-px pitch.
site
